title: Adaptive security intake: rightsized SLAs, regulator-aware routing, and evidence bundling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and large prospects frequently submit security and regulatory requests (SOC2 readiness, GDPR/DPA clarifications, HIPAA scoping, custom vendor questionnaires). Our current intake is manual, one-size-fits-all SLAs, and routes many items to the same triage queue, causing slow response times and inconsistent commitments. This leads to lost deal momentum and unpredictable engineering/SE load.

Goal: Build an adaptive intake workflow that: 1) automatically classifies incoming security/compliance asks by regulation, urgency, and contractual tier; 2) assigns a rightsized SLA and route (self-serve evidence bundle, security SME, legal review, or delivery engineering) based on that classification; and 3) provides an auto-assembled evidence bundle and prefilled questionnaire responses where possible to reduce manual work. The system should integrate with existing ticketing and evidence stores and produce metrics for latency, SLA attainment, and staff effort reduction.
background: We currently have multiple ad-hoc playbooks and several high-variance SLAs enforced manually by the PM/team. Similar initiatives in the product backlog focus on triage scorecards and intake gates, but none automate evidence assembly or regulator-aware routing. Sales and Customer Success escalate high-value RFPs which require faster SLAs. Engineering reports frequent interruptions from incoming questionnaire requests that could be handled by pre-built evidence bundles.
proposed_solution: 1) Classification layer: lightweight classifier (keyword + rule-based + ML fallback) that tags each request with regulation(s), data residency concern, customer tier, and question complexity. 2) SLA engine: mapping table that converts tags into an SLA and routing action (self-serve, SME review, legal, engineering). 3) Evidence bundler: pre-curated document sets (SOC2 report excerpts, ISO attestation summaries, redacted architecture diagrams, DPA clauses) and a templated questionnaire responder that merges with a per-customer variable set. 4) Operator UI in Console: a triage dashboard showing incoming items, predicted SLA, confidence, and recommended action; allow overrides and audit logs. 5) Integration: hooks to Zendesk/Github/Linear for ticket creation, Confluence/Drive for evidence retrieval, and Slack for SME notifications.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Classification accuracy: top-1 tag accuracy >= 85% on a sample of 200 historical tickets; false-negative regulator misses < 5%.
2) SLA assignment: 4 configured SLA tiers (Self-Serve 72h, Standard 10 business days, Priority 3 business days, Contracted 24-48h) correctly applied for >= 95% of test cases.
3) Evidence bundling: For 3 common request templates (SOC2 summary, GDPR DPA excerpt, HIPAA scoping checklist) the bundler produces a complete artifact bundle within 30 seconds for 90% of cases.
4) Routing: Automated routing reduces manual triage touches by 40% in the pilot org.
5) Metrics: Dashboard reports SLA attainment, mean time to first response, and pre-assembled evidence usage.
6) Legal & Security sign-off obtained before release to pilot customers.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (pilot, 4 weeks): Build classifier rules and a minimal SLA mapping; pilot with Sales & Security team; manual evidence bundling with admin-assisted assembly.
Phase 2 (expand, 6 weeks): Add ML classifier improvements, integrate evidence store for automated assembly of top 3 templates, expose triage dashboard in Console; run with 2 pilot customers and internal SEs.
Phase 3 (scale, 4 weeks): Add additional templates, performance and reliability hardening, enable automatic ticket creation and SLA enforcement, public docs for self-serve customers.
QA: include regression tests on classifier, evidence bundle integrity checks, and monitoring alerts for SLA breaches.
KPIs: SLA attainment, reduction in SE/Engineering interrupt time, deal win acceleration (measured qualitatively by AE feedback).
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Classifier mislabels high-sensitivity requests (HIPAA) and routes them incorrectly. Mitigation: low-confidence routing sends to human SME and logs flagged cases; restrict auto-assembly for any HIPAA-labeled item until legal sign-off.
Risk: Evidence bundler includes sensitive PII. Mitigation: redaction rules, templates only include pre-approved redacted artifacts, and bundler must respect data residency tags.
Risk: Overpromising SLAs causes operational stress. Mitigation: make SLA table configurable by contract and start conservative for pilot customers; add quota/burst controls.
Risk: Integration complexity with Drive/Confluence causing missing artifacts. Mitigation: fallback to manual attachment workflow and instrument missing-asset alerts to ticket owner.
implementation_notes: Start with rulebook written in YAML that maps keywords and headers to tags. Create a small training set from last 12 months of inbound requests (anonymized). Use existing evidence docs stored in /drive/ComplianceKit as initial bundle sources. Build triage UI as a new Console view under "Security Requests" that calls a new intake API (ENG-23145).
